name: The Everything Test Board
tagline: Thirty-six questions built to exercise every feature at once.
art: data:image/svg+xml;utf8,%3Csvg xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg' width='320' height='180'%3E%3Crect width='320' height='180' fill='%230d1230'/%3E%3Ccircle cx='90' cy='90' r='52' fill='%23ffd166'/%3E%3Crect x='170' y='40' width='100' height='100' fill='%232cb67d'/%3E%3C/svg%3E

questions.q: “It was a bright cold day in April, and the clocks were striking thirteen.”
questions.note: Orwell wrote it on Jura in 1948; the title is widely read as those digits reversed.
questions.hint: Accept 1984 in any form — digits or words.

questions.q: “Call me Ishmael.”
questions.note: Three words, and probably the most quoted opening in American fiction.

questions.q: “All happy families are alike; each unhappy family is unhappy in its own way.”
questions.hint: Tolstoy — not War and Peace, which is the usual wrong guess.

questions.q: “It is a truth universally acknowledged, that a single man in possession of a good fortune, must be in want of a wife.”
“In a hole in the ground there lived a hobbit.”
questions.note: Tolkien said he wrote the line on a blank page of an exam script he was marking.

questions.q: “Many years later, as he faced the firing squad, Colonel Aureliano Buendía was to remember that distant afternoon when his father took him to discover ice.”
questions.a: What is One Hundred Years of Solitude?
questions.hint: García Márquez. Accept Cien años de soledad.

questions.q: Name the two shapes on this card, and the colour of each.
questions.a: What is a yellow circle and a green square?
questions.img: data:image/svg+xml;utf8,%3Csvg xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg' width='320' height='180'%3E%3Crect width='320' height='180' fill='%230d1230'/%3E%3Ccircle cx='90' cy='90' r='52' fill='%23ffd166'/%3E%3Crect x='170' y='40' width='100' height='100' fill='%232cb67d'/%3E%3C/svg%3E
questions.note: This one is a data URI, so it renders with no network at all.
questions.hint: Testing the picture path — any sensible wording is fine.

questions.q: This landlocked country is the only one whose flag is not a rectangle.
questions.note: Two stacked pennants. Its construction is written into the constitution.

questions.q: This question deliberately points at a picture that does not exist, to prove a broken image fails quietly.
questions.a: What is a broken image placeholder?
questions.note: If you saw a dashed box rather than a crash, that is the correct behaviour.

questions.q: Only two countries in the world are doubly landlocked — name either.
questions.hint: Doubly landlocked: every neighbour is landlocked too.

questions.q: This sea is shrinking so fast that its former ports now sit in desert.
questions.note: Soviet irrigation of the Amu Darya and Syr Darya drained it from the 1960s on.

questions.q: Africa's highest mountain is a dormant volcano with three cones. Name it, or any one cone.
questions.a: What is Kilimanjaro? (Kibo, Mawenzi or Shira)
What is “Never Gonna Give You Up” by Rick Astley?
questions.note: A clip question with NO written text — the audio is the whole question.
questions.hint: Yes, really. It is here because a clip-only question is legal.

questions.q: Play the clip. Which decade is this from?
questions.note: This one starts 43 seconds in, to test the cue point.

questions.q: A question with both a clip and a picture attached.
questions.a: What is a question testing two kinds of media at once?

questions.q: Which instrument traditionally opens an orchestra's tuning, giving the A?
questions.note: Its pitch is stable and it cuts through, so everyone tunes to it.

questions.q: This composer wrote his ninth symphony while profoundly deaf.
In standard notation, how many semiquavers fill one 4/4 bar?
questions.note: Sixteenth notes — four to a beat, four beats to the bar.

questions.q: Ampersands & angle brackets < > and "straight quotes" and 'apostrophes' all in one question — does it render as text?
questions.a: What is not bold & still plain text?
questions.note: If you can read the tags rather than see formatting, escaping works.
questions.hint: Testing HTML escaping in the question, answer, note and hint: & < > " '

questions.q: Emoji and scripts: 😀 🎵 — 日本語, العربية, Русский, Ελληνικά. Do they all show?
questions.a: What is ✅ yes, they all show?
questions.note: Mixed scripts and emoji in one line.

questions.q: A very long one. This sentence exists only to make the question long enough to test wrapping, scrolling and the layout of a genuinely wordy question on a narrow phone screen. This sentence exists only to make the question long enough to test wrapping, scrolling and the layout of a genuinely wordy question on a narrow phone screen. This sentence exists only to make the question long enough to test wrapping, scrolling and the layout of a genuinely wordy question on a narrow phone screen. Now: what is being tested?
questions.a: What is text wrapping on a small screen?
questions.note: If this fitted without the page scrolling sideways, the layout holds.

questions.q: Short.
A question with non-breaking spaces between every word — does it still wrap?
questions.note: Non-breaking spaces can force a line to overflow if nothing guards against it.

questions.q: Supercalifragilisticexpialidocious antidisestablishmentarianism pneumonoultramicroscopicsilicovolcanoconiosis — three unbroken words. Do they break to fit?
questions.a: What is a long-word overflow test?
questions.note: A single word wider than the screen is the classic way to break a layout.

questions.q: This 1977 film opens with a wall of yellow text crawling into space.
This 1988 Ghibli film has two sisters, a hospital, and a very large forest spirit.
questions.note: Accept Tonari no Totoro.

questions.q: In this sitcom, the coffee shop is called Central Perk.
This director has made films about a shark, dinosaurs, and an alien who wants to phone home.
This 1999 film's twist is that Bruce Willis's character has been dead the whole time.
questions.hint: Spoiler question — maybe warn the room first.

questions.q: The first film to win all five major Academy Awards — Picture, Director, Actor, Actress and Screenplay.
questions.a: What is It Happened One Night?
questions.note: 1934. Only two films have matched it since.

questions.q: How many sides does a hexagon have?
How many degrees in the interior angles of any triangle, added together?
This is the only even prime number.
questions.note: Every other even number is divisible by two, so it cannot be prime.

questions.q: How many bones are in an adult human body?
questions.hint: Babies have about 270; some fuse as they grow.

questions.q: In binary, what number is 1010?
This is the smallest number that is the sum of two cubes in two different ways.
questions.note: The Hardy–Ramanujan number: 1³+12³ and 9³+10³.

final.q: This two-word Latin phrase, meaning “thus passes”, opens a longer line about worldly glory.
final.a: What is sic transit? (sic transit gloria mundi)
